expected_behavior.rubric: A correct answer explains that code after an await runs outside the original action's transaction, and fixes it by wrapping every state mutation that happens after the await (this.items = items and this.loading = false) inside runInAction, showing the corrected code rather than only describing the change.
pass_criteria: Shows the corrected code wrapping the post-await assignments (this.items = items and this.loading = false) inside runInAction(() => { ... }), or restructures the method as a flow generator that achieves the same effect
States that code after an await runs outside the original action's own transaction, which is why the bare assignments need to re-enter via runInAction (or flow)
fail_criteria: Recommends disabling or loosening enforceActions (e.g. configuring it to 'never' or 'never' equivalent) instead of wrapping the post-await mutations in runInAction -- mentioning that only to warn against it is not a failure
Leaves this.items = items or this.loading = false as bare, unwrapped assignments after the await with no runInAction or flow restructuring

calibration.known_wrong: Easiest fix: just set `configure({ enforceActions: 'never' })` in your app setup so MobX stops complaining about mutations outside actions. Then you can leave fetchItems exactly as it is -- the assignments after the await will still update the observable fields and trigger reactions, MobX just won't enforce the action-boundary rule anymore, which saves you from having to wrap anything in runInAction.
calibration.vague: You should make sure the state updates after the await happen inside an action so MobX can properly track them, otherwise you might run into issues with enforceActions.
calibration.subtle_wrong: The important part is that `this.items` gets set correctly, so I wrapped just that one in runInAction: `runInAction(() => { this.items = items; })`. I left `this.loading = false` as a plain assignment right after since it's just a boolean flag and not the actual data -- that keeps the change minimal and the loading indicator still clears in practice even without wrapping it.

calibration.known_wrong: Simplest fix: pass a changing key prop from the parent, like `<ItemList key={store.items.length} store={store} />`, so React remounts ItemList whenever the length changes. That forces a fresh render with the current value without having to touch MobX wiring at all.
calibration.vague: Something about how the component is hooked up to the store isn't quite right -- you probably need to set up the MobX integration for this component so it responds to changes.
calibration.subtle_wrong: The fix is to wrap the parent component that renders ItemList in observer, since that's where store gets passed down from -- once the parent is observed, MobX should propagate the re-render down to ItemList whenever store.items changes, so I left ItemList itself as a plain function component.
